title: Postdoctoral Scholar - Economics of Coastal Hazards and Resilience
description:
Postdoctoral Scholar – Economics of Coastal Hazards and
Resilience

Vacancy Number: PD-0035
Position Number: PD0038
Location of Workplace: Main UNCW Campus

Brief Summary of Work for this Position:
The Cameron School of Business at the University of North Carolina
Wilmington invites applications for a postdoctoral scholar in the
Department of Economics and Finance. This is a 12-month, full-time,
temporary non-faculty research position, with potential renewal
subject to university policies and available funding.
The postdoctoral scholar will work with Professor Meghan Millea on
the economics research thrust of the National Science
Foundation-funded Coastal Hazards, Economic Prosperity, and
Resilience (CHEER) research hub. CHEER brings together engineers,
economists, and social scientists to investigate hurricane risk,
recovery, and resilience in coastal communities. The economics
thrust examines household and community responses to hurricane
risk, including insurance decisions, hazard mitigation, adaptation,
and the economic consequences of disasters, with an emphasis on
eastern North Carolina.
The primary responsibility of the postdoctoral scholar is to
conduct research. Activities include developing and applying
quantitative economic methods, assembling and analyzing data,
interpreting results, preparing manuscripts and presentations, and
collaborating with researchers across institutions and disciplines.
The position may also involve research proposal development,
mentoring students, and engaging with community partners to connect
research findings with practical needs.

Appointment Description:
This is a 12-month, full-time, temporary non-faculty research
position, with potential renewal subject to university policies and
available funding.

Minimum Education and Experience Requirements:

Ph.D. in Economics, Applied Economics, Environmental or
Resource Economics, or a closely related field by the appointment
start date.

Ph.D. or equivalent doctorate in one of the fields listed above
and conferred before the appointment start date, but no more than
five (5) years prior to the appointment start date.
Exceptions to the 5-year degree requirement may be waived in
exceptional circumstances.




Research experience in applied quantitative analysis, including
econometric or computational methods.
Demonstrated ability to conduct independent research and
communicate findings in writing and presentations.
Ability to collaborate on interdisciplinary research
projects.



Preferred Education, Knowledge, Skills &
Experience:

Research experience in environmental economics, natural
hazards, disaster risk, insurance, adaptation, or economic
resilience.
Experience with spatial analysis, applied econometrics,
economic modeling, or computable general equilibrium methods.
Experience working with large or geographically detailed
datasets and collaborating with researchers from other
disciplines.
Record of scholarly publications or manuscripts in progress and
interest in research that informs policy and community
decision-making.

Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit:
The Department of Economics and Finance at the University of North
Carolina Wilmington, located in the vibrant coastal city of
Wilmington, North Carolina, offers four Bachelor of Science in
Business Administration concentrations: Economics, Finance,
Financial Technology (FinTech), and Real Estate. The department
also administers the Bachelor of Arts in Economics and the Master
of Science in Finance programs. In addition, faculty play an
integral role in supporting both the Master of Business
Administration (MBA) and the International MBA, a joint program
offered in collaboration with our international partner
universities.
The department fosters an engaging and experiential learning
environment through student organizations, competitive academic
opportunities such as the College Fed Challenge and CFA Institute
Research Challenge, the student-managed investment fund,
undergraduate honors research, and other high-impact learning
experiences. Faculty are equally committed to advancing scholarship
with a growing research portfolio and a strong culture of
collaboration that enhances teaching, research, and service.

University Information:
The University of North Carolina Wilmington, the state's coastal
university, is dedicated to the integration of teaching, mentoring,
research and service. Widely acknowledged for its world-class
faculty and staff and continuously recognized at a national level
for scholarly excellence and affordability, UNCW offers a powerful
academic experience that stimulates creative inquiry and critical
thinking.

A public institution with nearly 18,000 students, UNCW offers a
full range of baccalaureate- and graduate-level programs, as well
as doctoral degrees in educational leadership, marine biology,
nursing practice and psychology; and many distance learning
options, including clinical research, an accelerated RN-to-BSN
program, an Executive M.B.A. program structured for working
professionals, and the nation's only bachelor's degree program
focused on coastal engineering.

The university's efforts to advance research and scholarly
activities have earned UNCW the elevated designation of "Doctoral
Universities: High Research Activity" institution (R2 University)
by the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher
Education.

UNCW has been part of the University of North Carolina System since
1969.
